target_customer: E-commerce merchants in Egypt and the wider MENA region that pay per parcel for delivery and fulfillment
problem: Most delivery providers in the region used manual dispatch. ShipBlu sells delivery and fulfillment run by software and optimization algorithms.
business_model: Per shipment logistics and fulfillment fees, with payout and cash on delivery services
product_category: E-commerce logistics, last mile delivery and fulfillment

founders.name: Ali Nasser
education: B.Sc. Construction Engineering, American University in Cairo

founders.name: Ahmed ElKawass
education: B.A. Politics and Economics, Northumbria University

founders.name: Abdelrahman Hosny
education: Master's in Computer Science and Engineering, UConn
PhD in Computer Science in progress, Brown University
founders.background_notes: Focus on combinatorial optimization. Source: YC company page.

competitors.name: Bosta
competitors.what: Egyptian last mile delivery for e-commerce using a freelance driver network
competitors.funding_then: Series A of about $6.4M to $6.7M (outlets differ)

competitors.name: Flextock
competitors.what: Egyptian e-commerce fulfillment startup also backed by Flexport

technical_complexity.rationale: Routing and dispatch optimization with a merchant API and tracking is standard logistics software, but running a physical courier network is operationally hard.

defensibility.rationale: Merchant integrations and operating density help, but several funded rivals served the same merchants and couriers are not exclusive.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A 2022 Last Mile Experts analysis says Aramex led Egyptian last mile volumes by a wide margin. No source shows an incumbent copying ShipBlu.

market_need_then: Fast growing e-commerce in MENA with fragmented, manual delivery and a preference for cash on delivery. ShipBlu signed more than 40 merchants in its first month after August 2021 launch per TechCrunch.

identity.visual_style: Blue themed identity; the 'Blu' suffix carries into the myBlu app
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and efficiency focused: 'Ship Smarter .. Grow Faster'

branding.brand_signature: Blue identity and the 'Blu' product family (myBlu)

brand_strength.rationale: Coherent blue and 'Blu' family naming, but it is a B2B logistics brand with no press or community about the brand itself found.

outcome_analysis: ShipBlu raised a pre-seed and a $2.4M seed in 2021 from regional and global backers, launched operations in August 2021 and grew to about 300 people per the YC page. No acquisition or shutdown found. Third party profiles claim large revenue but are unverified. It operates against funded local rivals in a growing market, so the outcome is a scaling operator with undisclosed later funding.
notes: CB Insights lists total funding of $2.53M, slightly above the $2.4M seed, which is unverified and implies a small additional amount; no later round was found, so coverage is partial. A third party AI visibility profile claims $17.1M revenue in 2024 and 51 to 200 staff, which conflicts with the YC page team size of about 300 and is unverified. The confidence label is high because founders, competitors and funding are all sourced.
